title: Living ashtpadi 7
hook: choose your company as you'd choose food
tomorrow: Ashtpadi 8, salok: the one who knows God

segments.voice: Yesterday, abhimaan: pride rubbed out, wisdom coming into view. Your line was ego leaves quietly. Today, ashtpadi seven, lived.

Most of us think quite hard about food. We read labels. We notice when we've eaten badly for a week and feel sluggish. But company? Mostly it just happens to us: whoever's at work, whoever's in the group chat, whoever the feed serves up at midnight. We'd never let a vending machine choose all our meals. We often let chance choose all our company. Ashtpadi seven says that company feeds the inner life the way food feeds the body. So it's worth choosing.
screen: `WE READ THE LABELS ON FOOD.` → `COMPANY JUST HAPPENS TO US.` → `IT FEEDS US ALL THE SAME.`

segments.voice: Through the eight stanzas of ashtpadi seven, the phrase saadh kai sang, in the company of the holy, comes back again and again, each time with something new. The face grows bright. The grime washes off. Pride is rubbed out. Wisdom comes into view. God is felt near. And further on, two lines worth carrying out the door. Saadh kai sang dusman sabh meet: in the holy company, enemies all become friends. Meet is the word for a friend. And: in the holy company, there's no enmity toward anyone. That's a striking claim from a hard century. Guru Arjan himself was later arrested and executed under the Mughal authorities in Lahore, and Sikhs remember him as the first of their martyr Gurus. The man who wrote these lines knew what enemies were, and still he says: in good company, enmity loosens. So what does living this mean? Not dropping everyone who isn't saintly; Sikh teaching is clear that the Guru's house is open to all. It means paying attention to where your inner food comes from. Who leaves you lighter, and who leaves you heavier? Where is the Name remembered, and where is it mocked? Then one small choice toward the lighter table, the way you'd choose a real meal over a bag of chips. Not once in a lifetime. This week.
screen: `SAADH KAI SANG, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · `MEET: ENEMIES BECOME FRIENDS.` · `WRITTEN BY A GURU WHO KNEW ENEMIES.` · `ONE SMALL CHOICE, THIS WEEK.` · then, large: `CHOOSE YOUR COMPANY.`

segments.voice: Let your week ahead appear in your mind, day by day, and find one gap, an evening, a lunch, a morning walk, where a good person or a good place could go: a gurdwara, a library, a park bench with a wise friend. You're not deciding anything forever, only choosing one meal. Sit quietly with that choice, and notice whether it already feels lighter.
Meet, a friend. Company feeds the inner life as food feeds the body, and in the holy company, the stanza says, even enemies become meet.
Your line: choose your company. Company is food for the inner life, and worth a little care. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 465 COUNTS.` → `ASHTPADI 7, LIVED.` → `TOMORROW: ASHTPADI 8, SALOK: THE ONE WHO KNOWS GOD.`

howItsDone: Many Sikhs make a habit of joining the sangat each week, often on Sundays in the diaspora, and of keeping friends who support their remembrance of the Name.

trapdoor: what you thought: holy company is a feeling you hope to bump into.
what it means: it's something you choose, the way you'd choose good food.
what a scholar hears: Guru Arjan composed Sukhmani before his execution in Lahore in 1606, under the Mughal emperor Jahangir; the lines on enmity read differently against that history.

chat.says: Does choosing good company mean I should cut off friends who aren't very spiritual?
options: No. The Guru's house is open to all; it means choosing where your inner food comes from.
Yes, the Guru's house is only for the holy, so others shouldn't be welcomed in.
No, company doesn't matter at all; only what you do alone counts for anything.
chat.meaning: Ashtpadi seven says company feeds the inner life. Living it means choosing well, while the Guru's house stays open to all.
